baseline_models.focus_anchor: The definite masculine plural active participle al-mujrimin, governed by 'an, is the sole overt nominal focus.
baseline_models.mechanism: The offense branch reads the participle as an agentive classification: a definite collectivity is identified by enacted guilt, while the absent governor leaves only their status as the topic or relational object.

activation_trace.role: Guilt and offense supply the direct culpable-agent classification carried by al-mujrimin.

changed_reading.before: A minimally specified phrase: 'about the criminals.'
changed_reading.after: A definite culpable collective is held at discursive distance and made the object of concern or inquiry.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The Form IV active participle mujrim in the definite plural, read through the root's earning and causing-to-incur branch.
baseline_models.mechanism: The form can profile agents as bringing an acquired burden upon themselves or others, so criminality appears as an incurred result rather than an innate type.

activation_trace.role: Earning and causing another to incur supply active acquisition as the latent mechanism of mujrim.

changed_reading.before: People bearing a generic offense label.
changed_reading.after: Agents who acquire, produce, or incur the burden by which they are classified.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Al-mujrimin read through the cutting and harvesting branch of j-r-m, with 'an also marking relational distance or aboutness.
baseline_models.mechanism: The phrase can faintly image a collective defined by cutting or being cut out of relation; the construction supplies distance but does not decide whether they sever or are severed.

activation_trace.role: Cutting off and harvesting supply a separation mechanism that the prepositional distance can host.

changed_reading.after: A collective whose culpability may be imaged as enacted severance or as having been cut out from relation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Al-mujrimin read through the branch of a completed and cut-off span of time.
baseline_models.mechanism: The plural is provisionally viewed as people at the completed, severed end of a temporal span; this is a root-branch activation rather than a direct gloss of the participle.

activation_trace.role: Completed and cut-off time supplies a latent endpoint model for the named collective.

changed_reading.after: People named from the far side of a completed interval, when their course can be viewed as closed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus root's acquisition branch joins the immediately preceding sequence of what each self earns and the right-backed pledge that holds it. Mujrim thus becomes an agent whose acquisitions have matured into enforceable liability.

activation_trace.role: Earning and causing to incur turn the focus classification into an acquired burden.
Seeking and obtaining a gain supplies the concrete acquisition that can accrue against each self.
A security held for a right supplies the enforceable hold produced by what was acquired.

structural_cues: 74:38 places earning and being held in pledge immediately before the exception in 74:39 and the garden inquiry in 74:40-41.
The universal 'every self' is partitioned before the focus collective is named.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies acquisition and a pledge held for a right; I infer that the acquisition constitutes the claim for which the self is held. Alternatively, the pledge may image detention without a strict debt mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The focus names people who commit offenses.
changed_reading.after: The focus names agents whose own acquisitions have become an enforceable claim against them; criminality is accrued liability, not merely a label.

context_deltas.mechanism: The elliptical focus phrase is a discourse hinge. Reciprocal third-person inquiry becomes a second-person question about the route into Saqar and then a first-person plural answer, so a class spoken about becomes a speaking, self-describing party.

activation_trace.role: The offense branch identifies the party whose culpability is about to be tested in speech.
Mutual questioning supplies the reciprocal inquiry for which 'an al-mujrimin is the topical hinge.
Penetrating a path supplies the content of the direct causal question addressed to the group.
Uttered speech supplies the group's answer and turns the classified party into narrators of their own case.

structural_cues: 74:40 uses third-person reciprocal questioning, 74:41 supplies only 'about the mujrimin,' 74:42 addresses 'you' in the plural, and 74:43 answers 'we.'
The fragment occupies the exact boundary between observation from the gardens and testimony from Saqar.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the person shifts and the inquiry-speech sequence; I infer that the ellipsis stages a cross-boundary hearing in which identification becomes self-indictment. It may instead be rhetorical reported dialogue rather than a literal hearing.

changed_reading.before: The criminals are a static third-person topic.
changed_reading.after: The phrase pivots from talk about a culpable class to direct causal interrogation and that class's own plural testimony.

context_deltas.mechanism: The active acquisition potential of mujrim is reorganized as a path-dependent formation: insertion into a route is answered by repeated modes of being, entry into a shared current, and an arriving endpoint.

activation_trace.role: Earning and causing to incur let the participle denote an accumulated course rather than a fixed essence.
Inserting one thing into another supplies entry into the route whose causes the question seeks.
Occurrence and presence in time supply the repeated state expressed across the group's answer.
Entering an affair or discourse supplies active participation in a shared current rather than isolated error.
Arrival supplies the endpoint that closes the repeated course narrated in the preceding verses.

structural_cues: The causal question in 74:42 is answered by four coordinated clauses in 74:43-46, three of them carrying repeated forms of kana.
The sequence ends with hatta and an arrival in 74:47, giving the account a bounded trajectory.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies insertion, repeated states, collective wading, and arrival; I infer a causal arrow from habitual participation to the acquired mujrim condition. Alternatively, the clauses may list evidence of an already fixed status rather than narrate its formation.

changed_reading.before: A mujrim is a person marked by a punctual offense.
changed_reading.after: A mujrim is formed along a repeated route of omissions, collective participation, and denial that continues until its endpoint arrives.

context_deltas.mechanism: The cutting branch of j-r-m becomes relational: the focus group stands outside a named companionship, reports absence from worship and feeding, and finally cannot be joined by intercession. Their culpability is patterned disconnection across communal, ritual, and material bonds.

activation_trace.role: Cutting off and harvesting supply the focus image of severed relation.
Companionship and sustained association supply the contrasting group membership from which the focus group is separated.
The specified worship supplies one denied axis of attachment in the group's account.
Feeding another supplies the material-social bond the group says it did not maintain.
Joining one thing to its counterpart supplies the final joining that no longer benefits the severed group.

structural_cues: The exception of the companions of the right precedes the naming of al-mujrimin, creating a membership contrast.
The group's ritual and feeding omissions are followed by the explicit failure of intercession in 74:48.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies companionship, worship, feeding, and failed joining; I infer that these are axes of attachment whose rupture activates the cutting branch of j-r-m. They may instead be independent offenses with no single severance mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The focus class is separated only by a generic moral verdict.
changed_reading.after: The class is defined through severed participation: outside sustaining companionship, worship, material care, and finally beneficial joining.

context_deltas.mechanism: The completed-time branch of j-r-m is activated by a bounded day of account and by certainty arriving after the group's past-tense narrative. The label is heard retrospectively, after a mutable course has become a closed record.

activation_trace.role: Completed and cut-off time supplies the focus group's endpoint profile.
A duration of time supplies the bounded temporal field in which reckoning is denied.
Accounting and recompense supply the retrospective evaluation attached to that day.
Coming and arrival supply the event that terminates the narrated interval.
Settled knowledge with doubt removed supplies the irreversible clarity reached at the endpoint.

structural_cues: 74:43-46 narrates prior states and acts, while hatta in 74:47 marks a terminal boundary.
The statement that intercession no longer benefits them follows immediately in 74:48.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a day, accounting, arrival, and settled certainty; I infer that certainty's arrival closes the interval in which the group's course could change. Alternatively, al-yaqin may name an event without activating the temporal branch of j-r-m.

changed_reading.before: Al-mujrimin denotes an atemporal kind of person.
changed_reading.after: Al-mujrimin is a retrospective name for people whose course and account have reached a completed, no-longer-revisable boundary.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because harvest residue is a material noun-image and does not directly gloss the active participle. It remains anchored in the focus root's residue branch and in the packet's paired language of preserving and leaving nothing; downstream prose should present it only as a processing or harvest overlay, not as a replacement translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Al-mujrimin read through j-r-m's image of what falls or is gathered after harvest.

activation_trace.role: Harvest residue and dried fruit matter supply a post-separation material image for the focus collective.
What remains of a thing supplies the residue category that Saqar is said not to preserve.
Leaving a thing supplies the second negated remainder operation in the processing image.

changed_reading.before: The focus refers only to juridically classified offenders.
changed_reading.after: The group can also be imaged as post-harvest material delivered to a process whose defining threat is that no remainder is preserved or left.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the voice-resonance branch is guarded and branch-distant, so it cannot redefine mujrim lexically. It remains anchored in the focus root and in the packet's uttered, circulating, collective denial; downstream prose should qualify it as an acoustic-social overlay on culpability.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Al-mujrimin read through the j-r-m branch of voice resonance emerging from bodily mass.

activation_trace.role: Voice resonance emerging from the body supplies an acoustic mode in which the focus classification becomes public.
A saying that spreads among people supplies circulation beyond a private judgment.
Entering discourse with others supplies collective participation in the voiced current.
Attributing falsehood supplies the specific denial externalized through that shared discourse.

changed_reading.before: Culpability is a silent interior or legal condition.
changed_reading.after: Culpability also takes bodily voice and social circulation as the group enters a shared discourse of denial.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because bodily mass and clear color are remote j-r-m branches, not ordinary senses of mujrim. It remains anchored by two focus branches and by the packet's human-surface, heat-marking, and unveiling images; downstream prose should render it as an embodied visibility analogy, never as the lexical meaning of al-mujrimin.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Al-mujrimin read through j-r-m's bodily-mass and clarified-color branches.

activation_trace.role: Bodily bulk and shaped mass supply the embodied substrate on which the focus status can become visible.
Color becoming clear supplies the disclosure of a previously non-visible classification.
Heat that alters color supplies the process by which an inward status is marked outwardly.
Visible skin and surface supply the location where the heat-mark becomes legible.
Removing a covering supplies the broader disclosure movement that makes the marked body readable.

changed_reading.before: The focus names an abstract moral category.
changed_reading.after: The category can be overlaid as embodied mass whose concealed record is exposed as a visibly altered surface.

strongest_changes: The earning branch of j-r-m, joined to acquisition and pledge in 74:38, changes generic offense into accrued and enforceable liability.
The person shift across 74:40-43 changes 'about the mujrimin' from a static topic into the hinge of direct questioning and self-testimony.

The route, repeated states, collective wading, and terminal arrival change mujrim from a punctual label into a formed trajectory, while companionship and failed joining expose its relational severance.
summary.what_was_special: A one-root elliptical fragment became the surah's switching point between classification and testimony. The same focus inventory supported juridical accrual, social severance, temporal closure, and carefully contained material or acoustic overlays without requiring those readings to collapse into one interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The omitted governor of 'an leaves open how tightly 74:41 belongs to reciprocal inquiry versus the direct question that follows.
The cutting image does not decide whether the group actively severs bonds, is severed by judgment, or sustains both directions.
The temporal, harvest-residue, voice, and surface models are branch-backed mechanisms but should not be promoted to replacement lexical glosses.
